title: 12O Banderazo: national multi-city protests over government policies
location: Buenos Aires (Obelisk and other locations); contemporaneous reports identify demonstrations in La Plata, Rosario, Bariloche, Córdoba, Mendoza and other cities
scope: Nationally coordinated multi-site demonstration, promoted through social-media hashtags; city-level organization and counts require further review.
organizer: Public social-media call using #12O and related hashtags; opposition figures participated or promoted it. Exact organizing group is not established.
participants_original: El Territorio reported thousands of people at the multi-city banderazo, centered on the Buenos Aires Obelisk; it separately described dozens in Posadas. No precise venue-by-venue count was found.
threshold_50_evidence: El Territorio's contemporary report describes thousands at the multi-city national banderazo and identifies the Obelisk as its epicenter. This is qualitative support for a 50+ event at the national-action level, but attendance by individual city remains unresolved.

start_date.summary: Both contemporaneous articles describe the banderazo held Monday 12 October.

location.summary: Reports identify the Buenos Aires Obelisk as the central gathering and describe demonstrations in multiple provinces/cities.

state_target.summary: Reports describe opposition to national government COVID restrictions, judicial reform and other federal policy and institutional choices.

demands.summary: The articles identify opposition to quarantine restrictions and the national judicial reform/court process, alongside other complaints.

participants_original.summary: El Territorio reports thousands across multiple sites and separately says dozens attended in Posadas; no exact overall or Buenos Aires count is given.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The qualitative report of thousands at the nationally coordinated action supports the threshold at the event level; venue-specific group counts remain unknown.

state_response.summary: No state-response category is established in the retained event evidence; unknown.

notes: Participation by opposition politicians does not by itself make this an excluded electoral rally: the reports also identify demands directed at national policies and institutions. The campaign nature, national event boundary, and city-level attendance remain open; do not split or merge city gatherings without evidence. Buenos Aires Times and Canal 26 accounts are retained as discovery only because written-story origins are ambiguous; see S005 and S007.
open_questions: Was the national call a single nationally organized event or several locally organized gatherings with shared slogans?
What was the attendance at Buenos Aires and each other reported city separately?
Were any state response actions reported outside the accounts reviewed?

title: ATE national work stoppage and public mobilization over the government salary offer
location: Buenos Aires (Obelisk to Congress) and other locations across Argentina
scope: Nationally organized union action with strike, public demonstrations and virtual university-teacher stoppages; whether all locations form one event under the original event rules needs review.
organizer: Asociación Trabajadores del Estado (ATE), with participation or support announced by other state-sector unions including Fesprosa and Conadu Histórica.
participants_original: TN reports workers gathering at the Obelisk and demonstrations in multiple provinces. It gives no street-action participant count; 354 refers to delegates at a planning meeting, not protesters.
threshold_50_evidence: A public march and national mobilization are reported, but no size estimate establishes that any single gathering reached 50. Pending threshold.

start_date.summary: TN reports the ATE national strike and mobilization on 6 October.

location.summary: TN places the Buenos Aires gathering at the Obelisk with a caravan toward Congress and reports activity in the provinces.

state_target.summary: ATE rejected the national government's 7% public-employee salary offer and sought reopened collective bargaining.

demands.summary: The reported demands concern public-sector wage levels and reopening salary negotiations.

participants_original.summary: The report says workers gathered and additional unions joined; no crowd figure is stated. The 354 delegates were meeting participants, not street protesters.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No 50+ street attendance is reported; threshold remains pending.

state_response.summary: No coding evidence found for the listed state-response categories; unknown.

notes: ATE's 30 September article is an advance announcement; TN's 6 October report is the evidence that the action occurred. Do not use the 354-delegate planning-meeting count as the protest count. Virtual work stoppages alone are not a public gathering.
open_questions: Did any single public gathering reach 50 participants?
Can a national union action spanning venues be coded as one event under the original rules?
What, if any, state response occurred at the street gathering?

title: Social-organization march to the Ministry of Social Development for jobs and expanded assistance
location: Buenos Aires: Plaza Constitución, Avenida 9 de Julio and Ministry of Social Development
scope: One reported march to a national ministry; possible prior similar action in September was described as a separate, completed protest.
organizer: Social-organization delegates announced the action. TN names several groups, but a Polo Obrero leader disputed that the people threatening the overnight encampment represented his organization; exact site organizer remains unresolved.
participants_original: TN describes the march as large and says it lasted more than three hours; no numerical crowd estimate is reported.
threshold_50_evidence: TN calls it a large/massive public protest involving multiple social organizations and reports a march lasting over three hours. This qualitative contemporary description supports 50+ attendance; no exact count is available.

start_date.summary: The contemporary article is dated 7 October and describes the march that afternoon.

end_date.summary: TN reports the protest action ended around 20:30 on 7 October after an agreement.

location.summary: The march began at Plaza Constitución, proceeded along Avenida 9 de Julio and ended at the Ministry of Social Development.

state_target.summary: Protesters sought a response from national Government officials at the Ministry of Social Development.

demands.summary: Reported demands include jobs, wage levels, increased assistance-program benefits and resources for food programs.

participants_original.summary: The report describes a large march by social organizations but provides no numerical estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Contemporary report calls the public march large/massive and describes multiple organizations participating over several hours.

state_response.summary: Government authorities received the organizers, reached an agreement and the protest ended; other listed response categories are unknown.

notes: Do not treat the meeting with government or resulting agreement as proving all demands were met; accommodation here records receipt and an agreement. A prior similar protest about three weeks earlier is described as separate and completed, not as continuation.
open_questions: Which organizations actually led the October 7 crowd, given the reported identity dispute?
What was the reported agreement and which demands did it address?
Were any arrests or dispersal actions reported?

title: Mapuche land occupation at El Foyel and court-ordered eviction
scope: A five-day occupation of a privately owned parcel that ended with a judicially ordered eviction; any related road blockade was a separate action by another group.
organizer: Members of Lof Gallardo Calfú, as reported by TN; no formal organizer identified.
participants_original: TN reports about 40 people occupied the parcel at the start; it does not report a crowd of 50 or more later.
threshold_50_evidence: The only reported estimate is about 40 occupants; no source establishes that the gathering reached 50. Pending threshold.

start_date.summary: TN says the five-day land occupation began on Thursday 15 October.

end_date.summary: TN reports the eviction was carried out on Monday 19 October.

location.summary: The report places the occupied 400-hectare parcel in El Foyel, Río Negro.

state_target.summary: A court order led to the eviction, but the source does not establish whether the community's demand was directed at government policy or a private land dispute.

demands.summary: Occupants characterized the occupation as recovery of land they said had been taken from their community; state-policy connection is unresolved.

participants_original.summary: TN reports about 40 occupants at the land site; this is below 50 as reported, and no later occupancy figure is supplied.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Available figure is about 40 occupants. No 50+ gathering is documented.

protester_violence.summary: TN says a vehicle used by its news crew was attacked, but does not describe violence by protesters against the state; coding remains unknown.

state_response.summary: TN reports a court-ordered eviction and four detentions; no other listed response is established.

notes: The reporter says most people left voluntarily after dialogue with authorities, while four were detained during the eviction. The incident involving the TN vehicle does not establish protester violence against the state. The reported occupation began in October and is not a known cross-month continuation.
open_questions: Was the land claim tied to a public land or Indigenous policy demand, or was it solely a private title dispute?
Did attendance ever exceed the reported initial figure of about 40?

title: Route 40 blockade opposing the El Foyel eviction
location: National Route 40 near Villa Mascardi, Río Negro
scope: A separate road blockade by Lof Lafken Winkul Mapu in response to the eviction of Lof Gallardo Calfú at El Foyel.
organizer: Members of Lof Lafken Winkul Mapu; the report distinguishes this group from the occupants of the El Foyel parcel.
participants_original: TN says about ten people were involved in the road interruption; no larger crowd is reported.
threshold_50_evidence: The only available account says about ten people were involved, below 50; no evidence shows a larger gathering.

start_date.summary: TN reports the route action on 19 October after the El Foyel eviction.

location.summary: The road blockade was near Villa Mascardi on Route 40 between Bariloche and El Bolsón.

state_target.summary: The report says the blockade protested a court-ordered eviction; whether this constitutes a qualifying state-policy demand is unresolved.

demands.summary: The stated immediate objective was opposition to the El Foyel eviction; no separate public-policy demand is documented.

participants_original.summary: TN reports about ten people involved in the traffic interruption.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The available estimate is about ten; no 50+ crowd is documented.

protester_violence.summary: No evidence of violence against the state is recorded; unknown.

state_response.summary: A federal judge ordered security forces to clear the route, but execution at the gathering is not established in this passage.

notes: TN reports blockade participants carried slings and stones were thrown at a media crew at a separate location near the governor's arrival. The report does not establish violence against state agents at the roadblock. Source gives an approximate group of about ten, below the inclusion threshold.
open_questions: Was a larger crowd present at any stage?
Was the response order executed at the protest site?
Does this action demand state policy redress or only oppose a case-specific eviction?

title: Protest outside El Bolsón police station seeking release of four detainees
location: Outside Police Station 12, El Bolsón, Río Negro
scope: A distinct evening protest after the El Foyel eviction and detention of four Mapuche community members.
organizer: Unidentified local demonstrators; no named organizing body is given.
participants_original: Diario Río Negro describes a group of demonstrators but supplies no number.
threshold_50_evidence: A report says a group gathered outside the police station but gives no participant estimate; 50+ remains unverified.

start_date.summary: The report says the police-station gathering occurred on the evening after the 19 October eviction.

location.summary: Demonstrators gathered outside Police Station 12 in El Bolsón.

state_target.summary: Demonstrators sought release of four people held by police.

demands.summary: The text reports a demand for release of four detainees but does not provide a category-specific rationale.

participants_original.summary: The regional report describes a group but does not estimate attendance.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No participant number or clear qualitative evidence of 50+ attendance is reported.

state_response.summary: No response to this separate demonstration is reported; unknown.

notes: The four detentions were reported as arising during the separate land eviction. Do not automatically code them as arrests made in response to the police-station protest. A Bariloche demonstration was called for the following day, but occurrence was not confirmed in the body-read material.
open_questions: Did the planned Bariloche demonstration on 20 October actually occur?
